newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia mulls Yugoslav offer on dual citizenship.
newsitem.headline: Croatia mulls Yugoslav offer on dual citizenship.

text.p: Croatia said on Monday it was considering a proposal made by neighbouring Yugoslavia to agree a treaty giving residents of Eastern Slavonia dual citizenship after Croatian rule is restored in the enclave.
"Our experts from various ministries are considering good and bad sides of such an agreement," the state news agency HINA quoted Foreign Minister Mate Granic as saying.
Yugoslavia sent a draft of the treaty to Zagreb for consideration last Friday. No details of its terms were made public.

"We shall give it thorough consideration, from the aspect of our national interest," Granic said. It is in Croatia's interest that all Croats living in Yugoslavia have a regulated right to dual citizenship, he added.

Western diplomats in the region have been urging such a treaty, saying it would help avert an exodus of frightened ethnic Serbs before Zagreb takes over fertile Eastern Slavonia, now the last Serb enclave in Croatia.
Eastern Slavonia was one of three areas where local Serbs seized power in a 1991 revolt against Croatia's independence from Yugoslavia.
It is now under U.N. supervision and will revert to Croatian government rule with guarantees for minority rights after elections on April 13.
